diagnostic_tracker.title: Coin Counters — Day 1 Diagnostic Checklist
diagnostic_tracker.when_used: During Lesson 1, while children are in the partner estimate-then-count phase of the Action segment.
diagnostic_tracker.usage_notes: Walk between pairs during the estimation activity. For each child, tick the columns where you see clear evidence; leave blank if not yet observed. 'Estimate within 3 of actual' is the diagnostic signal for emerging quantity-sense. 'Counts on from a given number' captures A6.8 explicitly. Children with blanks across the first three columns may need small-group re-loop on Lesson 1 before continuing.

formative_trackers.title: Coin Counters — Lesson 2 Formative Tracker (Partners of 5)
formative_trackers.when_used: During Lesson 2, while children are in the Partner Hunt game.
formative_trackers.usage_notes: Walk between pairs during Partner Hunt. The 'instant vs counting' columns capture recall versus computation — important for A6.11's 'recall' wording. Children who tick 'Cannot find missing partner' need 1:1 reteach with the cube tower visible.

columns: Models the start of the story with materials

formative_trackers.usage_notes: The 'Deals one at a time' column is the key strategy signal — children who scoop piles but get the right answer are using calculation, not the K-appropriate dealing strategy. The leftover round flushes them out.

summative_rubric.title: Coin Counters — Summative Rubric

rows.expectation_text: estimate the number of objects in small collections and check by counting

levels.descriptor: With adult prompting, names a number when shown a small collection but the estimate is far from the actual count.
Names an estimate that is sometimes within 5 of the actual; counts to check with support.
Independently estimates within 3 of the actual count and verifies by counting.
Estimates within 2 of the actual; explains the strategy ('I saw a bunch and added a couple more').

rows.expectation_text: count to 20 by 1s, starting from any number

levels.descriptor: Counts to 10 starting from 1; cannot count from any other start.
Counts to 20 starting from 1; counts on from a number with prompting.
Counts to 20 starting from any given number 0-15 without restarting.
Counts to 20 from any start; volunteers count-back from a given number.

rows.expectation_text: solve equal-share problems using concrete materials

levels.descriptor: Distributes objects unevenly; does not check fairness.
Shares evenly when totals divide cleanly; gives up on leftover scenarios.
Deals one at a time, checks each plate; articulates a leftover plan.
Deals fluently; explains why dealing works for any total; offers multiple leftover plans.

rows.expectation_text: describe relationships between any two numbers from 0 to 20

levels.descriptor: Identifies which of two numbers is bigger only with strong adult prompting; cannot articulate the relationship in words.
Identifies bigger / smaller for two numbers within 0-10 with prompting; struggles with numbers 11-20.
Independently describes more, less, equal, or 1-more / 1-less relationships between any two numbers 0-20.
Articulates multiple relationships ('5 is more than 3 AND less than 8 AND 2 less than 7'); spontaneously uses comparison language in everyday counting.

rows.expectation_text: recall addition facts to 5 and related subtraction facts

levels.descriptor: Counts to find sums to 5; cannot recall any partner of 5 instantly.
Recalls 1-2 partners of 5 (typically 4+1 or 2+3); counts up for the rest.
Recalls all 6 partners of 5 instantly and connects each + with its related −.
Recalls partners of 5 fluently; extends spontaneously to partners of 6 or 7.

rows.expectation_text: solve situations involving addition and subtraction to 10 using concrete materials

levels.descriptor: Models the start with materials but cannot decide which operation; guesses.
Chooses correctly when keywords are obvious; struggles with 'altogether' vs 'left'.
Listens to a story, picks the right operation, models with cubes or coins, writes the equation.
Maps story to operation fluently; writes the equation before modelling; explains the keyword cue.

rows.expectation_text: identify and explore the value of Canadian coins to 25¢ and coins and bills to $10

levels.descriptor: Names some coins by colour but mixes up the dime and nickel; does not yet attach values.
Names the four coins reliably; states the value when prompted with the chart.
Names all four coins on sight, states their values without the chart, and pays for a 5¢/10¢/25¢ snack with a single matching coin.
Pays for a price multiple ways using coin combinations (e.g., 10¢ as 2 nickels OR 1 dime); explains why combinations are equivalent.

summative_rubric.purpose: End-of-unit summative rubric covering all 7 expectations (A6.7-A6.13). Used by the teacher to score each child against four levels (Beginning, Developing, Achieving, Exceeding). Achieving = on track for K end-of-year expectations.
summative_rubric.usage_notes: Apply this rubric to each child's combined evidence: the Lesson 1 diagnostic + L2/L3/L4 formative trackers + Lesson 5 summative worksheet. The score is holistic — a child whose summative worksheet was perfect but whose tracker shows operation-choice errors should be Level 3, not Level 4. Record level 1-4 per expectation; the level achieved is the lowest of the relevant evidence sources for that expectation.
summative_rubric.layout_description: One letter page, landscape orientation. Title at top. Body is a 4-column rubric grid (Level 1, Level 2, Level 3, Level 4) with one row per expectation (7 rows). Each cell ~1.8in × 1.2in, descriptor text in 9pt font.

summative_task_script.title: Lesson 5 Summative Task — Coin Counters at the Snack Shop
summative_task_script.purpose: End-of-unit summative assessment for the Coin Counters unit. Captures evidence for A6.13 (coin recognition + payment) explicitly and A6.11/A6.12 (coin value composition) through the multi-coin combination prompts. Used as the headline scoring artifact alongside the formative trackers.
administration_steps: Bring children back to the carpet after the small-group rotations on Day 5.
Hold up the worksheet and walk through the three parts: (1) coin matching grid, (2) snack-shop pay scenes, (3) pay 10 cents three different ways.
Distribute one worksheet per child. Allow 15 minutes for completion.
Walk around and record per-child evidence on the Lesson 5 formative tracker (recognition, value, single-coin payment, multi-coin combination).
Collect worksheets and score against the rubric. Map total to level: 9-10/10 = Level 4; 7-8 = Level 3; 5-6 = Level 2; 0-4 = Level 1.
summative_task_script.scoring_guidance: Part 1 (4 matching pairs) captures A6.13 coin recognition. Part 2 (3 priced items) captures A6.13 payment selection. Part 3 (3 different combinations totalling 10 cents) captures A6.11/A6.12 coin value composition. Total score out of 10. Map to summative rubric: 9-10 = Level 4 Exceeding; 7-8 = Level 3 Achieving; 5-6 = Level 2 Developing; 0-4 = Level 1 Beginning.

evidence_per_expectation.A6.12: Lesson 3 formative tracker. Mid-unit Numerals 0-10 Check-In worksheet.
